Steps the Nymphes LFO 1 through its four wave shapes, shown by the four lamps marked L, H, T and B
Steps the Nymphes LFO 2 through its four wave shapes, shown by the four lamps marked L, H, T and B
Switches key sync for LFO 1 on and off, shown by the lamp marked key
Switches key sync for LFO 2 on and off, shown by the lamp marked key
Switches the Nymphes sustain state on and off, shown by the lamp marked on
Switches legato on and off, shown by the lamp marked on
Chooses the play mode, one of poly, uniA, uniB, tri, duo and mono, with a lamp under each name
Opens a file chooser and reads a .nym patch file into the sliders
Opens a file chooser and writes the slider settings out as a .nym patch file; cancelling that chooser crashes Rack
Puts the LFO 2 modulation depths on the red sliders, and keeps whatever is set there under that source
Puts the modulation wheel depths on the red sliders, and keeps whatever is set there under that source
Puts the velocity depths on the red sliders, and keeps whatever is set there under that source
Puts the aftertouch depths on the red sliders, and keeps whatever is set there under that source
Switches the program change between the user and the factory bank, shown by the two lamps marked user and factory
Chooses the program to send, 0 to 48, read out on the display as a bank letter and a number from one to seven
Sends a MIDI program change for the program that has been dialled up
Takes the program number over from the knob while a cable is in, 0 to 10V across 0 to 127; a number above 48 has 48 taken off it and switches to the factory bank
A rising edge above 1V sends the program change, which the send button also does
Note — nothing goes out or comes in until a MIDI device is chosen in both selectors at the top of the panel; both come up reading No device, and the module is silent until then
Note — the two device selectors are MIDI widgets rather than knobs or jacks, so a click on one of them cannot reach this help; the upper pair is the input and the lower pair the output
Note — the red sliders carry one modulation source at a time; the four buttons marked lfo2, wheel, vel and after choose which, and each source keeps a set of depths of its own
Note — every slider moves on its own when the matching control is turned on the synth, so the panel follows the hardware as well as driving it
Note — controller values go out at about a hundred a second in total, so a fast sweep of a slider reaches the synth as a coarser ramp than it looks on screen
Note — the numbers under each slider read out the value last sent for that control

NymphesControl.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 7c97127, the head of the repository. Six commits carry version 2.1.0 and four of them change the source, so the build was settled from the binary twice over: the controller-number table at commit 8e2251e swapped two blocks of CC numbers, and the installed dylib carries the swapped table as a run of 32-bit integers (36,37,39,40,41,45,46,47,48,49,50,51,58,59 and 12,5,15,16,14,81,4,8,79,80,82,83,20,21), which rules out everything before it; and commit 7c97127 moved the font load out of the display widgets' constructors into their draw methods, and in the installed binary the only two calls to Window::loadFont sit inside DisplayWidget::draw at 0x11264 and VerySmallDisplayWidget::draw at 0x11a50, with neither constructor calling it. That is the head. Three faults. The save button dereferences the file chooser's result before testing it for null (std::string pathStr = path, with the if (path) test on the line after), so cancelling the Save dialog constructs a std::string from a null pointer and takes Rack down with it; the load button has the same code with the test in the right place. The module declares a MOD_SOURCE1 parameter whose addParam call is commented out in the widget, so it has a ParamQuantity, occupies parameter index 76 and can never be clicked or turned - it gets no line here for that reason. And every controller parameter is configured 0 to 128 while the value sent is clamped to 0 to 127, so the last step of every slider's travel sends nothing new. The controller numbers in the lines are read straight from the nymphes_cc_map table and the index arithmetic that reaches it (learnedCcs[j+44] for the twenty-eight main controls and the reverb, LFO 2, wheel and volume ones, learnedCcs[i+8] for the thirty-six modulation depths). The fourth oscillator slider is lettered chord on the MOD panel and left blank on the main panel; it carries controller 16 there, which is the same control, so both lines name it chord. Sending is throttled by a 0.0005 second rate limiter and a further count of twenty passes between messages.
